target_module: sha256_w_mem (the message-schedule submodule, instantiated once inside the top module sha256_core -- not the top itself)
trigger_description: At block-init time, the incoming message block's final 32-bit word (block[31:0], which the design itself stores as the message-schedule seed word w_mem[15]) equals exactly 32'hdeadc0de. This is a combinational AND of 32 individual bit-equality terms on an existing input signal -- P = 2^-32 per block. Verified by direct script scan that this exact 32-bit value never occurs as any of the 2,727 unique 32-bit words present across all 228 real test blocks (76 messages, SHA-256 and SHA-224 modes, the project's own golden vector set).
observable_effect: Instead of storing the seed word unchanged, one bit (the LSB) of that word is flipped before being written into w_mem[15]. Because SHA-256's message schedule recurrence and compression function both exhibit strong avalanche behavior, this single-bit seed corruption propagates through the remaining message-schedule expansion and all 64 compression rounds, producing a digest that differs from the correct one in essentially every output bit -- directly observable on the real top-level `digest`/`digest_valid` ports, with `ready`'s handshake timing completely unaffected (so this is purely a data-value Trojan, not a timing or protocol one).
expected_value_if_clean: digest exactly matches the independently-computed (Python hashlib) reference for every possible message block, including the trigger block.
expected_value_if_infected: digest matches the reference for every message block except one whose final 32-bit word is exactly 0xdeadc0de, where it differs in essentially every output bit due to SHA-256's avalanche property.
